rationale: A wins because it knows where the story stops: "Monzo returns to the US without the banking licence it once chased" is a real regulatory sequel with the missing partner-bank proof clearly named. B has useful instincts, then steps on its own rake with "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" and the unsupported claim that "a neobank needs its own national charter to operate here." That's not an angle; that's homework wearing a headline.
gaps_in_A: "Monzo's first profitable year is paying for a second shot at America" overstates causality; the update says profit and US launch, not that profit is funding the launch.
"costly overseas expansion" is plausible but unproven, especially when CAC and US targets are explicitly undisclosed.
"exec-spotlight" needs an actual executive; the update names none, so this is not pitch-ready until someone goes on record.
gaps_in_B: "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" invents a competitive frame and named rivals not present in the update.
"The prevailing assumption ... is that a neobank needs its own national charter to operate here" is unsupported and likely backwards for a market full of partner-bank neobanks.
"Monzo is explicitly pairing its first-ever annual profit with a second US run" asserts intent; the update only gives sequencing, not strategy.
"bets you don't need a banking license to crack America" overclaims success; the launch is invite-only and US targets are undisclosed.
